glossary.definition: Stock Keeping Unit - a unique identifier for each distinct product in inventory
Machine-readable representation of data in visual format, typically printed on product labels
Universal Product Code - a 12-digit barcode standard used primarily in North America
European Article Number - a 13-digit barcode standard used internationally
A high-density barcode symbology capable of encoding full ASCII character set
The inventory level at which a new order should be placed to replenish stock
The standard amount to order when inventory reaches the reorder point
Manual correction to inventory quantities to account for discrepancies, damage, or loss
A commercial document issued to a supplier indicating products, quantities, and agreed prices
The process of accepting and recording incoming inventory shipments
A completed sales event consisting of one or more products sold to a customer
The total monetary value of all inventory on hand, calculated using cost prices
Loss of inventory due to theft, damage, miscounting, or other factors
The location and system where sales transactions are completed
System operation capability without active internet connection, with later synchronization
Security approach restricting system access based on user roles and permissions
Chronological record of system activities and user actions for security and compliance
Automated notification when product quantity falls below the defined reorder point
The rate at which inventory is sold over a specific time period
Processing multiple products or quantities in a single receiving operation
